description: Workspaces Console: the secondary interface of every repository's command line. Commands, checks, findings, previews and decisions in VS Code, through each repository's own launcher.
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.descrip: Workspaces Console runs each repository's own command line, so it runs nothing in a workspace you have not trusted.
capabilities.virtualWorkspaces.descripti: Workspaces Console runs a command line that lives in a clone on this machine.

welcome.home.0:
Nothing is set up in this window yet. If you have installed Workspaces, open your workspace: File, Open Workspace from File, then choose workspaces.code-workspace in your workspaces folder. The short guide walks you through it.
[Open Getting Started](command:workspaces-console.openWalkthrough)
[Add Repository…](command:workspaces-console.addRepository)
[Refresh](command:workspaces-console.refresh)
welcome.home.1:
VS Code is asking whether you trust the folders in this window, and the Workspaces Console waits for your yes before it runs anything. If you or your organization put these folders here, trusting them is safe. Only you can decide.
[Trust this workspace](command:workspaces-console.trust)
[Open Getting Started](command:workspaces-console.openWalkthrough)
welcome.home.2:
The tools in this folder did not start yet, so there is nothing to show. The usual cause is that setup has not finished: one button finishes it. The Output panel says exactly why.
[Install everything](command:workspaces-console.setUpEverything)
[Show Output](command:workspaces-console.showOutput)
[Refresh](command:workspaces-console.refresh)
welcome.home.6:
ws-host has not been told to use this repository yet, so its command line cannot start. Enabling it lets ws-host install the programs the repository lists, from the addresses and checksums it names, and run its command line.
[Enable this repository](command:workspaces-console.enableProvider)
[Show Output](command:workspaces-console.showOutput)
welcome.home.3:
Something these tools need is not installed yet. One button installs everything and shows how far it has got; run `doctor` from the Command Palette to see exactly what is missing.
[Install everything](command:workspaces-console.setUpEverything)
[Show Output](command:workspaces-console.showOutput)
[Refresh](command:workspaces-console.refresh)
welcome.commands.4:
No folder in this window declares a command line for Workspaces Console.
[Refresh](command:workspaces-console.refresh)
welcome.commands.5:
This workspace is not trusted, so Workspaces Console runs nothing.
[Trust this workspace](command:workspaces-console.trust)

configuration.title: Workspaces Console
setting.launchers.description: Launcher file names to try at the root of a workspace folder that declares none in its own `.workspaces-host/provider.toml`. Only your own user settings are read; a workspace cannot name what Workspaces Console runs.
setting.checkOnSave.description: After a file is saved, run `check --changed` for its repository and show the findings in **Problems**.
setting.showAllCommands.description: Show the **All commands** view, the tree of every noun, command and resource of every command line. It is hidden by default because **Home** and the views each command line declares are where daily work is; the *Show All Commands* action in Home's `…` menu shows it for this session only.
setting.rowLimit.description: The most rows of one kind a view lists before it says how many more there are. **Find Resource** searches all of them.

walkthrough.title: Get started with Workspaces
walkthrough.description: Seven short steps, each one button. Nothing here needs a terminal.
walkthrough.home.title: This is your home base
walkthrough.home.description:
The Workspaces Console in the sidebar says what needs you and gives every step a button.
[Show Home](command:workspaces-console.showHome)
walkthrough.signIn.title: Sign in to GitHub
walkthrough.signIn.description:
Once. You get a short code and a web address; you never type a password here.
[Sign in to GitHub](command:workspaces-console.signIn)
walkthrough.setUp.title: Install everything
walkthrough.setUp.description:
One button installs the programs your repositories need and shows how far it has got.
[Set Up Everything](command:workspaces-console.setUpEverything)
walkthrough.addRepo.title: Add your repository
walkthrough.addRepo.description:
Type its address; it is copied here and kept up to date.
[Add Repository](command:workspaces-console.addRepository)
walkthrough.check.title: Check that it all works
walkthrough.check.description:
A green list means every program is in place; a yellow line says what to do.
[Check Environment](command:workspaces-console.doctor)
walkthrough.website.title: See the website on your computer
walkthrough.website.description:
Start it, then open it in your browser. Stop it when you are done.
[Start Service](command:workspaces-console.startService)
walkthrough.update.title: Keep everything current
walkthrough.update.description:
One button brings Workspaces, your repositories and their programs up to date, never touching your own changes.
[Update Everything](command:workspaces-console.updateEverything)
command.toggleSimpleViews.title: Show Every View
setting.simpleViews.description: Show only the everyday views a command line marks (Books and Papers, say) instead of every view it declares. On by default so a newcomer is not shown twenty views; the *Show Every View* action in Home's `…` menu shows all of them for this session only.
